frontier.hypothesis: Target's loop-2 preheader copy is produced by a pass that runs AFTER cse and combine and that our build reaches with different inputs - loop.c's strength-reduction preheader emission (emit_iv_add_mult) or regmove.c - not by any C-level construct. The symmetric chassis makes this decidable because both preheaders are then the same construct with different outcomes in the SAME dump.
frontier.mechanism: Both of target's preheaders end with `addu v0,a0,v1` (the strength-reduced giv init for `base + i`), which is loop.c output emitted into the preheader after cse/combine have run. If loop.c (or regmove.c) is what materialises the `addu a3,a0,zero` copy, then no preheader spelling can ever produce it - which is exactly what s11's 47 cells and s12's 23 symmetric-chassis cells measured - and the deciding input is the loop's giv/biv structure, not the addend expression. s12 additionally rules out the last C-level alternative (cse folding after the join is removed): the join cannot be removed, and jump2 will not re-merge a duplication.

Identify at which dump the `addu a3,a0,zero`-shaped copy would have to appear, and in the .loop dump compare loop 1's and loop 2's giv/biv records (they differ in outcome inside a single dump, so the deciding record is visible side by side). Do NOT re-probe any preheader addend spelling, declaration order, parameter homing, loop-body spelling, exit form, loop shape, or the base-destination local - all six are measured dead.

frontier.hypothesis: The residual is decided by which loop gets the ONE available purchase and target pays for neither - i.e. target's compiler produced both copies for free from a state our compiler never enters, and the difference is upstream of the function body in the TRANSLATION UNIT (declaration context, the math_Distance3D prototype, or struct/type shape), not in the function's statements at all.
frontier.mechanism: Twelve sessions have now measured every statement-level axis inside this function to a flat plateau while the instruction COUNT already matches target exactly (127 on chassis A). GCC 2.7.2's allocno ordering and cse hash tables are affected by things outside the function body - the number and order of preceding declarations in the TU (cf. the cc1-first-pass-scheduler-bug memory, where ~1400 lines of preceding decls changed cc1's behaviour on a trivial function), and the declared prototype of the called function (math_Distance3D's parameter types decide how its arguments are set up and therefore the tail's register pressure).
frontier.next_probe: Sweep the TU context rather than the function: (a) the math_Distance3D prototype in the header (s32* vs void* vs a struct pointer; 2 args vs 3) and whether its arguments are cast at the call site; (b) the position of func_80017848 within src/ings.c relative to its neighbours; (c) the presence/order of the file's preceding declarations. Re-score each with tmp/grind/func_80017848/s12/score.sh. This is the first axis in twelve sessions that is not inside the function body, and s12's flat plateau across every in-body region is the affirmative case for trying it. Note the scope constraint: only src/ings.c and include/ headers are touchable - do NOT touch the Makefile, linker script or pipeline txt files.
